title: Compare two boxed numbers

blocks.text: `==` on two references asks whether they point at **the same object**, not whether the objects hold the same value. `Integer.valueOf` returns a cached object for values from -128 to 127, so `==` on two `Integer`s often looks right in a quick test and then fails on bigger numbers. And a reference can be `null`, where calling a method on it throws a `NullPointerException`.
Write `BoxedEquality.sameValue(Integer a, Integer b)`. It returns `true` when both hold the same number, or when both are `null`; otherwise `false`.

cases.says: It compares small numbers by value.
Equal numbers outside -128..127 are the same value although they are different objects.
Two nulls are the same, and a null never equals a number.
